title: New hope after an old duty ends

captions.energy: Releasing an outdated pattern of involvement
captions.emotions: Feeling room for a new beginning

meaning: Your care can make room for hope when an earlier duty ends without ending involvement itself.
text: A familiar duty can come to an end and leave more space for closeness. In the physical position of Anahata, the Emperor expresses care through definite actions: agreeing arrangements, organising necessities and answering for what was promised. Death in energy encourages ending an outdated pattern that no longer brings warmth to you both. The Star in emotions gives a sense of opening possibility. The former arrangement need not be maintained endlessly out of loyalty to its form, and another way of being together becomes interesting. Hope offers room to search without requiring a repetition of the past.

Suppose you have prepared a large shared celebration for years and now recognise that the work displaced the pleasure of meeting. You cancel the usual list and agree on a small evening without visitors. **An ended duty can free attention for a living person.** Little is necessary: choose the time, communicate the change and prepare a comfortable place. Tenderness is recognised in freedom to try a different evening without proving its value through the amount of preparation or the former scale.

The difficulty is seeking relief only in cancellation. The earlier duties finish, but new involvement gains no concrete form. Empty waiting replaces hope, and the other person may not know where warmth is available now. One small promise kept can help: it need not restore the outdated duty, but shows that the wish to remain close is still present.
